name: Fernando Arendt
home: the streets inland from Pier Beach
life: “I still remember a nurse finding my village's actual spelling.” Thursday often includes a stop at the entrance to the Wash House, where Fernando stops for local notices even on a day without a load to wash.
voice: I kept a clinic letter because the doctor spelled our village correctly. Its date fills the last gap.
appearance: Fernando is easy to recognize by tightly curled gray hair and two dimples that appear only with a full smile. Usually dressed in an olive canvas jacket with a pressed flower kept in the clear back of a phone case, Fernando gives a little nod before asking a hard question when listening.
personality: Fernando enjoys bargaining, including over things already settled. It is partly a joke and partly a test of whether the other person feels able to say no.
agenda: To close the last gap using the village letter.
family: Keir Zhou is Fernando’s younger cousin. Fernando sets the time to leave. Keir picks the meeting place. It lets them stay close without turning a family visit into the loss of an entire day. They have both had stretches when that distinction mattered. Asked about *The margin reader*, Keir says, “I erased three lines before I understood. I've written down the one I remember.”
connections: Dana Harris. Old letters help the former spouse confirm dates without reopening the marriage.

reactions.response: Fernando waits for the patient to give a preferred public name before repeating it.
